title: Tenali Raman Tale 108

full_text:
King Krishnadevaraya, inflamed by a false intelligence report that a neighboring border governor had insulted the royal standard, leaped up from his throne in a fiery rage.
He drew his sword and shouted to his generals:
'Mobilize ten thousand cavalry immediately! We march at sunset to burn the governor’s citadel and put his garrison to the sword!'

Prime Minister Appaji and the senior ministers were terrified: they knew the border governor was loyal, and that the report was a deceptive rumor spread by enemy spies to provoke a destructive war.
Yet none dared speak against the King while his wrath was boiling.

Tenali Raman stepped forward, carrying a large brass pot of fresh, thick milk and an open charcoal brazier.
Tenali placed the brazier on the floor before the throne, set the pot of milk upon the coals, and blew the embers until they glowed red-hot.

Within minutes, the milk began to boil violently.
White foam rose rapidly up the sides of the brass pot, threatening to boil over and spill across the King's velvet throne carpet!
The King shouted in annoyance:
'Tenali! Look at the milk! It is boiling over! Take it off the fire before it ruins the carpet!'

Tenali stood calmly with folded hands, doing nothing.
The King leaped up, reached for a jug of cold water, and splashed three drops of cold water into the bubbling foam:
Instantly, the white foam subsided, the boiling quieted, and the milk settled peacefully inside the pot!

Tenali smiled with profound gentleness:
'Look, Maharaj!
When the milk was boiling violently with fiery heat, a single cup of cold water was enough to restore calm and save the carpet.
Your royal mind is currently boiling with the fiery heat of anger from an unverified rumor.
If you march your army today while your wrath is foaming, you will spill the blood of hundreds of innocent soldiers and ruin the carpet of your empire!
Pour three drops of cold patience upon your boiling heart. Wait three days. Verify the report.
If the governor is truly a traitor, your sword can strike him down on the fourth day just as easily as today.
But if you strike in haste, not all the tears in the world can bring a slain loyal servant back to life.'

King Krishnadevaraya looked at the settled milk, then at his drawn sword.
The fever of anger broke.
The King sheathed his weapon: 'Tenali, thy pot of milk has saved an empire from folly.'

Three days later, messengers arrived with proof that the report was an enemy forgery! The loyal border governor was innocent.
The King embraced Tenali, acknowledging that patience is the true shield of a righteous ruler.
moral: Haste and anger ruin the finest plans; patient waiting allows boiling fury to cool into wisdom.
